stem: How many distinct arrangements can be made using all the letters of the word BALLOON?

per_option_rationale.rationale: BALLOON has 7 letters with L repeated twice and O repeated twice. Distinct arrangements = 7! / (2! x 2!) = 5040 / 4 = 1260.
Computed 7! = 5040 as if all letters were distinct, ignoring the two repeated pairs L and O.
Divided 7! by only one 2! instead of two, giving 5040 / 2 = 2520, accounting for one repeated letter but missing the second.
Divided 7! by (2! + 2!) = 4 rather than by (2! x 2!) = 4, a coincidental value here; or equivalently computed 7! / 8 = 630 by treating denominators additively.

explanation: BALLOON: B, A, L, L, O, O, N - 7 letters with L(2) and O(2). Distinct arrangements = 7! / (2! x 2!) = 5040 / 4 = 1260.

explanation_sections.punchline: Two repeated pairs (L and O) each reduce the count by a factor of 2!, giving 7! / (2! x 2!) = 1260.
explanation_sections.approach: Classify as arrangements of n objects with repetitions. Step 1 - list every letter: B(1), A(1), L(2), O(2), N(1). Step 2 - write the formula: n! / (r1! x r2! x ...) = 7! / (2! x 2!). Step 3 - compute: 5040 / 4 = 1260.
explanation_sections.lesson: For every repeated letter frequency k, divide by k!. If two letters each repeat twice, divide by 2! x 2! = 4, not by 2! + 2! = 4 (numerically same here but the principle differs for other frequencies).
explanation_sections.timing: 60-70 s. Fastest path: cancel 7! / 2! = 2520 then halve again for the second repeat: 2520 / 2 = 1260. Trap: forgetting the second repeated letter O and stopping at 2520.
